description:
About the Position

Wageningen University & Research advertises a PhD position on impact evaluation of climate policies in agricultural and forest landscapes, within the EU Horizon project PolicyForClimate. The project assesses how climate policies - from payment schemes to regulation - change land-use decisions and emissions across agricultural and forest landscapes, combining econometric impact evaluation with land-systems modelling and case studies across Europe and partner regions. The doctoral candidate will design quasi-experimental evaluations, work with policy and geospatial datasets, and contribute to project publications.

Wageningen is a global leader in agri-food, environmental and land research, and the doctoral position offers a unique combination of policy-econometrics training and land-systems science. The employment is a salaried four-year PhD position under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement, embedded in a project consortium spanning European research institutes and policy partners, with travel to project meetings and case-study regions.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in environmental economics, environmental science, geography, agricultural economics or a related discipline, with solid quantitative training and interest in policy evaluation. Experience with statistical evaluation methods, GIS or land-use data is an advantage. Applications are submitted through the WUR careers site, and the closing date for applications is 4 November 2026.

Highlights

  • PhD on climate-policy impact evaluation (EU Horizon PolicyForClimate)
  • Agricultural and forest landscape focus
  • Quasi-experimental evaluation and land-systems modelling
  • European consortium with policy partners
  • Salaried four-year position per the CAO-NU agreement (WUR)
  • Closing date: 4 November 2026

About Wageningen University & Research

Wageningen University & Research is a Dutch institution focused on life sciences, agriculture, food and the environment. It combines university education with research addressing sustainable food systems and living environments. Its programmes and projects connect biological, environmental and social perspectives, supporting collaboration with academic institutions, industry and public organisations worldwide.
